memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The LORD said to Moses, "Do not be afraid of him, for I have delivered him into your hands, along with his whole army and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon." So they struck him down, together with his sons and his whole army, leaving them no survivors. And they took possession of his land. - Num 21:34-35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before the battle even began, God spoke a word of assurance: "Do not be afraid." The giant Og and his army may have looked overwhelming, but the outcome was already settled in the counsel of God. Victory was promised before a single sword was raised.

What a comfort it is when God goes ahead of us. He did not ask Israel to summon up courage from within themselves. He gave them courage by pointing to what He had already decided to do. Their confidence rested not in their own strength but in His promise.

We should read the outcome soberly, remembering that this was a specific judgment within God's plan for that land and time, not a pattern for us to imitate. Yet the word that steadied Israel still steadies us. Again and again, God tells His people, "Do not be afraid," and grounds that command in His own presence and power.

Whatever giant stands before you, hear the same word today. You do not face it alone or in your own strength. The Lord goes before you, and in Christ He has already won the decisive victory over your greatest enemies of sin and death (1 Cor 15:57). Do not be afraid.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What fear is God asking you to surrender to Him today?
2. How does knowing God goes before you change the way you face challenges?
3. Where do you need to hear afresh the words "Do not be afraid"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when fear rises up within me, speak Your steadying word: do not be afraid. Thank You that You go before me and have already won the victory in Christ. Amen.
